intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene on chromosome X.

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome
checks.explanation: The abstract states the conclusion directly.

checks.claim: The TBX22 gene is located on chromosome X.
checks.evidence_quote: X-linked cleft palate (CPX) is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the TBX22 transcription factor
checks.explanation: The abstract calls the disorder X-linked. The chromosome location is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977). Pauws et al. (2013) described it as an X-linked, CHARGE-like syndrome that is allelic to X-linked cleft palate with or without ankyloglossia, and noted that its phenotype extends to sensorineural deafness and coloboma, features not previously associated with X-linked cleft palate.

checks.claim: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis.
checks.evidence_quote: A new syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis has been described.
checks.explanation: The six features match exactly. The eponym is just the later name for this syndrome.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) described Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome as an X-linked, CHARGE-like syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, of unknown etiology
checks.explanation: The abstract uses this exact description.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) described Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome as allelic to X-linked cleft palate with or without ankyloglossia.
checks.evidence_quote: X-linked cleft palate (CPX) is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the TBX22 transcription factor and is known to exhibit phenotypic variability, usually involving either a complete, partial or submucous cleft palate, with or without ankyloglossia.
checks.explanation: The word 'allelic' is not used. It follows directly because TBX22 is shown to cause both CPX and Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) noted that the phenotype of Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome extends to sensorineural deafness and coloboma, features not previously associated with X-linked cleft palate.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotype extends to additional features including sensorineural deafness and coloboma, which are suggested by the Tbx22 developmental expression pattern but not previously associated in CPX patients.

paragraphs.text: Pauws et al. (2013) referred to the disorder as X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome. Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) argued that the patients in the original family did not have CHARGE syndrome or association.

checks.claim: Pauws et al. (2013) referred to the disorder as X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: X-linked CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome and classic cleft palate with ankyloglossia result from TBX22 splicing mutations.
checks.explanation: The title uses this name for the disorder.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) argued that the patients in the original Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome family did not have CHARGE syndrome or association.
checks.evidence_quote: We do not think that the patients in this family have the Charge syndrome or association.
checks.explanation: The abstract says directly that the patients do not have CHARGE syndrome or association.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) described a family with a new syndrome of cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis. They stressed the need for accurate and complete family histories in cases of cleft palate and cleft lip/palate for genetic counseling and estimates of recurrence risk.

checks.evidence_quote: The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the new syndrome with these features. Its use of the family history to infer inheritance shows that a family was affected.

checks.claim: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) stressed the need for accurate and complete family histories in cases of cleft palate and cleft lip/palate for genetic counseling and estimates of recurrence risk.
checks.evidence_quote: The need for accurate and complete family histories in cases involving cleft palate and cleft lip/palate is discussed in relation to genetic counselling and recurrent risk estimates.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) carried out a follow-up study of the family they had reported in 1977 to assess the subsequent development of the patients and to determine whether they had CHARGE syndrome. The family had been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome, but the authors concluded that their patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Pauws et al. (2013) hypothesized that TBX22, the gene mutated in X-linked cleft palate, might be involved in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome of unknown etiology. They identified a novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T-A) that tracked with the phenotype in the family. In patients with classic X-linked cleft palate, they identified a novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G-A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G-A) in the same exon. In silico analysis predicted that all 3 variants abolish normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro splicing assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome. The authors concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome.

agent.process_note: All 5 papers are abstracts only, and I read every one in full. The causal gene, TBX22, and the c.593-5T>A mutation come from the Pauws et al. (2013) abstract. That abstract gives no family size, number of affected people, zygosity wording, intron number or chromosome location, and no HGNC reference data was supplied. So I left out the gene MIM number and the cytogenetic location, and in the intro I wrote only 'mutation' rather than 'hemizygous'. The Davenport et al. (1986) abstract is about ear anomalies in CHARGE syndrome. The Metlay et al. (1987) abstract reports a different family with CHARGE syndrome. Neither abstract mentions the Abruzzo-Erickson family, so I left both uncited. The 2 CPX splice variants (c.767+5G>A and c.767+1G>A) appear only in Molecular Genetics, not as allelic variants, because they were found in classic cleft palate patients.
